messages:
maria: Heads-up — planning to add a few new audit fields to the event schema this week. want quick eyes on retention/immutability implications before we land.
james: can you list the fields and their intended semantics? will any be PII?
sophia: CC compliance: important to know retention buckets per org and whether customers can request exports. also need to surface which fields are customer-visible vs internal-only.
maria: proposed fields: `org_id`, `request_id`, `user_agent`, `event_hash`, `event_version`.
rahul: event_hash ok for tamper-detection but we need to decide signing vs hash-only. signing means we can prove origin with a KMS sig key.
maria: thinking: keep event_hash (sha256) for internal immutability checks + `signed_by_kms: true/false` when we have a KMS signature attached.
james: storage impact: signed payload adds ~512 bytes if we use RSA/PSS, smaller with ECDSA. prefer HSM-backed ECDSA via KMS to keep size small.
tara: from customers: they'd like an exportable audit bundle they can independently verify (not just trust us). so signature + public key verifiable bundle is ideal. :+1:
sophia: regulatory note: for some customers we need WORM-style retention (append-only, non-rewindable) for X years. footprint matters — we should separate hot access copies vs long-term archive.
rahul: storage design thought: write canonical JSON -> compute sha256 -> sign with per-customer wrapping key in KMS -> store signed blob in S3 with object lock/retention (WORM). metadata index in DynamoDB for fast queries.
james: question: per-customer KMS keys vs tenant-subkey approach? per-customer KMS is expensive operationally and increases key count.
maria: tradeoffs: per-customer KMS gives strongest isolation and auditability. alternative: single signing key + per-customer envelope keys (KMS wrap) so we can rotate signing key without re-signing everything.
sophia: compliance prefer per-customer root keys if they request it, but default can be platform-managed key with options to bring-your-own-key (BYOK).
tara: how will customers validate exports? a simple verifier script + public key should work. can we include a signed manifest with each export that lists file checksums and signature?
ahul: yes — export package: manifest.json (list of object keys + sha256), manifest.sig (signature). verifier checks checksums then verifies manifest.sig against our public key or customer's public key if BYOK.
maria: example manifest snippet:
```
{
  "bundle_version": "1",
  "objects": [
    {"key": "s3://redwood-audit/2026/03/12/obj-001.gz", "sha256": "..."},
    {"key": "...", "sha256": "..."}
  ],
  "signed_at": "2026-03-12T14:22:01Z"
}
```
james: ops note: to satisfy WORM we must set S3 Object Lock in governance/compliance mode and set bucket-level default retention OR use Glacier Vault Lock for archive. also make sure lifecycle rules don't accidentally expire objects before retention.
sophia: legal asks: record KMS key IDs used for signing in the manifest and in audit logs. that helps during eDiscovery.
rahul: KMS rotation: we should implement key hierarchy: master signing key -> rotate but keep previous public keys in key registry for verification of older exports. store public keys in a versioned key registry (signed as well).
tara: customer-facing event validation: which fields should be redacted on exported events? user_agent ok, but IPs might be PII for some customers.
maria: plan to add `redaction_level` metadata per org. default = `minimal` (no ip), `pii_removed`, `full_anonymized`.
sophia: ensure config UI + API for customers to select retention/rotation policy and redaction level. also require acceptance of export SLA (we may take up to N hours for large archives).
james: implementation checklist idea:
- schema v2 spec doc
- storage design doc (S3 + Object Lock + index)
- KMS key hierarchy & rotation plan
- export manifest + verifier tool
- customer config endpoints + consent flows
maria: creating GH issue: INFRA-1839, will paste link when done. tagging infra + compliance + cs.
audit-bot: INC-9723 created for "audit export validation & WORM retention plan" assigned to rahul, due 2026-03-19.
rahul: i'll prototype signer + manifest generator this week. can someone pair on verifier script? tara can help with CS testcases.
tara: happy to run through customer testcases and sample exports.
maria: ok thanks everyone. i'll PR schema changes after INFRA-1839 design doc lands. if no blockers by EOD Friday we'll schedule a canary export run next week. :rocket:
